name: Dubai
title: Thickness Measurement Dubai: Drydocks World & Jebel Ali
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Dubai at Drydocks World, Jebel Ali and anchorage: hull structure, pre-docking and renewal survey gauging for ships.
h1: Hull Gauging in Dubai for Ships at Drydocks World and Jebel Ali
intro: Dubai is a major maritime business centre: owners, ship managers and charterers run fleets from the city, and Drydocks World at Port Rashid docks some of the largest ships trading in the region. When a tanker or offshore unit is booked in for its renewal survey, or a container ship has a long call at Jebel Ali, we carry out ultrasonic thickness measurement in Dubai for the class survey, a CAP rating or the pre-docking steel estimate, with a team mobilised from India to the vessel.

highlights.p: Large tankers, gas carriers and offshore units dock at Port Rashid for renewal surveys, repairs and conversions. Gauging before the ship arrives firms up the steel list, and confirmation readings follow once the new plating is in.

Summer deck temperatures and humid, airless tanks slow every gauging job in Dubai. We plan tank entry, ventilation and work-rest cycles with the master and the yard so the programme holds through the hottest months.

highlights.h: Close to the managers who decide
highlights.p: Many technical managers running Gulf and Indian Ocean fleets work in Dubai. While the team is in the city for the ship, scope reviews and report walk-throughs can be held in person with the superintendent.

port.h: Dubai's ports and the ships that stay long enough to gauge
p: Dubai has two very different port areas. Jebel Ali, operated by DP World on the south-western edge of the emirate, is the largest container port in the Middle East and the gateway to the Jebel Ali Free Zone; its berths also handle bulk, break-bulk, ro-ro and liquid cargo. Closer to the city centre, Port Rashid (Mina Rashid) has moved away from cargo and now centres on its cruise terminal, while the neighbouring Drydocks World yard and Dubai Maritime City form the emirate's ship-repair and marine-services district.

Container ships on mainline services turn round quickly at Jebel Ali, so gauging there is usually confined to limited scopes, such as piping, a few ballast tanks or a pre-purchase sample, fitted into the port stay. The long stays happen at the yard. A tanker, bulk carrier or offshore vessel docked at Drydocks World for its renewal survey sits in dock or at a repair berth for days to weeks, and that is when the full thickness measurement programme is carried out. Ships lying at the Dubai anchorages awaiting a berth, new orders or a docking slot are another opportunity, reached by launch through the agent.

What sets Dubai apart is that decision-makers and steel are in one place. Owners from across the Gulf and the wider Indian Ocean bring ships here for repair because of the yard's large docks and its long record of offshore conversion work, and the technical managers approving renewal-survey work are often in the city too. That creates steady demand for pre-docking gauging to estimate steel renewal, for CAP work on older crude tankers, and for condition gauging when a ship changes hands or comes off charter. It also means a gauging report is often discussed the same day, face to face, by the people who will act on it.

facilities.h: Drydocks, berths and anchorages: where Dubai gauging takes place
p: Most full-scope gauging in Dubai takes place at Drydocks World, where ships are dry-docked or lie at repair berths with staging, lighting and gas-free certificates arranged by the yard. Work in dock has to fit the yard's sequence, because blasting, staging and steel renewal all compete for the same tanks. The TM plan is therefore agreed with the yard's project manager and the owner's superintendent before the ship arrives, and readings are taken in the order the tanks are released. Results showing substantial or excessive corrosion go to the superintendent the same day, so renewal can be ordered while the staging is still rigged and the class surveyor is still attending.

Outside the yard, gauging is done wherever the ship has a safe, gas-free window: at Jebel Ali berths during a longer call, at Mina Rashid on cruise turnaround days, or at anchorage. Smaller repair facilities in Dubai Maritime City handle tugs, supply boats and harbour craft, which need gauging at their own renewal surveys. For owners with ships at several UAE ports, Dubai is also a practical point from which to plan a sequence of jobs along the coast.
list: Drydocks World, Port Rashid — renewal-survey gauging, pre-docking steel estimates and confirmation readings on tankers, gas carriers, bulk carriers and offshore units in the large docks
Jebel Ali Port — limited-scope gauging and piping inspection on container ships, ro-ro and break-bulk vessels during longer port stays, with ISPS access through the agent
Dubai anchorages — launch-boat gauging for pre-purchase, on-hire and CAP sampling on tankers and bulkers held at anchor for a berth, fresh orders or a docking slot
Mina Rashid cruise terminal — piping and scrubber wash-water line checks on cruise ships during turnarounds in the winter cruise season
Dubai Maritime City — renewal gauging on tugs, workboats and offshore support vessels at the smaller repair facilities next to the main yard

context.h: PSC, fuel sulphur and Dubai's ship-management community
p: Ships calling at Jebel Ali are inspected by UAE port state control officers working within the Riyadh MoU, the regional regime the GCC states share. Structural findings such as wasted deck plating, holed air pipes, corroded ventilator coamings and wasted hatch coamings feature in detentions everywhere, and an owner who knows the ship's thickness margins is far better placed to answer them. The Gulf is not a sulphur emission control area; the applicable limit is the global 0.50% cap under MARPOL Annex VI regulation 14. Ships fitted with exhaust gas cleaning systems still trade here on high-sulphur fuel, and their wash-water and overboard piping corrodes quickly in warm seawater.

Dubai's importance for inspection is commercial as much as physical. A large community of ship managers, owners' representatives, charterers, P&I correspondents and marine surveyors works from the city, and decisions about which ship goes to which yard, or whether a 15-year-old tanker gets a CAP rating or goes for sale, are often taken here. The environment adds its own engineering case for gauging: summer air and sea temperatures, the Gulf's high salinity and dew-soaked nights all shorten coating life in ballast tanks and drive condensation corrosion in void spaces, cargo holds and under-deck structure.

jobs.h: Gauging scopes superintendents bring to Dubai
jobs.p: Dubai enquiries are usually tied either to a docking date at Port Rashid or to a commercial deadline such as a sale, a charter delivery or a vetting inspection. The scopes below are typical. Each one starts from the class survey requirements, the buyer's specification or the charterer's checklist, and is planned around the time the ship will actually spend in dock, alongside or at anchor.
list: Third renewal survey of a VLCC at Drydocks World: cargo and ballast tank structure, deck and bottom plating gauged to the ESP extent, with pre-docking readings sent ahead to fix the steel list.
Pre-docking gauging of an Aframax at the outer anchorage some weeks ahead of its docking, so plate quantities for renewal are settled with the yard before arrival.
Scrubber piping inspection in Dubai on a container ship during an extended call at Jebel Ali: wash-water, discharge and overboard lines, including the sections close to the shell penetration.
Off-charter hull gauging at Jebel Ali for a multipurpose or ro-ro vessel at redelivery, giving owner and charterer a measured record of deck, hold and tank-top condition.
Renewal-survey gauging of an anchor-handling tug supply vessel at a Dubai Maritime City yard, concentrating on the cargo deck, stern roller area, chain lockers and fuel and drill-water tanks.

logistics: Teams fly into Dubai International (DXB), which has frequent direct flights from India; Al Maktoum International at Dubai World Central, near Jebel Ali, is an alternative. Yard access at Drydocks World is arranged with the yard through the owner's site team, and port entry at Jebel Ali or Mina Rashid needs an ISPS gate pass requested by the ship's agent. Anchorage work is done by launch, also booked through the agent. UAE entry visas for the team are processed before departure, so we confirm the job early and follow the ship's ETA and docking date closely.

faqs.q: Will you work on a ship while Drydocks World has it in dock for repair?
faqs.a: Yes. A dry-dock stay is the best time for a full programme, because tanks are gas-free and staging is in place. We settle the TM plan with the yard's project manager and your superintendent, take readings in the order tanks are released, and report suspect areas daily so steel renewal can be added to the work list while the ship remains in the dock.

faqs.q: Is ship inspection in Dubai possible at anchorage rather than alongside?
faqs.a: For limited scopes, yes. Pre-purchase sampling, on-hire condition gauging and spot checks on deck plating, coamings and any tanks the crew can open are possible from a launch at the Dubai anchorages, provided the crew can make the tanks safe for entry. Full renewal-survey gauging needs dry-dock access to the bottom shell and the tanks, so it is normally done at the yard.

faqs.q: Does the Gulf heat change how a gauging job in Dubai is run?
faqs.a: It changes the planning rather than the method. Between June and September tank interiors and exposed decks get extremely hot, so we schedule tank entry for the cooler parts of the day, ask for forced ventilation and allow for work-rest cycles. The UAE also has a summer midday break for outdoor work, which we build into the daily programme on deck.

faqs.q: When should we brief you about a docking or inspection in Dubai?
faqs.a: Once the docking slot or inspection date is firm. The team travels from India, so visas and flights need lead time, and a TM plan prepared from the ship's drawings and previous gauging reports makes the work on board faster. For a renewal survey at Drydocks World, share the docking date and survey status with us at the same time as you confirm the yard booking.
